result.title: Synchronizing Cameras via 3D Object Relationships
result.summary: In this paper, we synchronize multiple videos of the same dynamic event through object relationships. Driven by dynamic reconstruction and novel view synthesis, many recent synchronization methods rely on pixel-level evidence, such as point correspondences across views or the photometric losses of a reconstructed scene. In dynamic scenes, however, fast motion and occlusions make the moving regions that carry much of the timing information hard to match across views. We thus propose to bring back the traditional wisdom that objects are reliable cues for global reasoning about cameras. Measured in 3D, the relationships between objects, such as the distance between two people, are stable across all views up to scale; they can serve as cues for alignment. To compare these relationships across cameras, we only need the identity of each object in every view, as the cues are relational. We obtain these identities by giving a vision-language model a few frames of every camera and prompting it to identify the objects in the scene. We then segment and track each identified object through every video with an open-vocabulary segmentor. To obtain the 3D locations of objects, we use a pretrained depth estimator. Where depth or segmentation fails, we complement these 3D cues with 2D motion from point tracks. Finally, we synchronize the cameras by finding the temporal offsets at which the cues of different cameras agree best, first for each camera pair and then for all cameras jointly with robust optimization. We evaluate our method on four standard benchmarks, outperforming the state of the art.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究多相机拍摄同一动态事件的时间同步：用 VLM 从少量帧中识别各视角中的物体，再由开放词表分割与跟踪、预训练深度与点轨迹得到 3D 关系线索，最后通过成对与联合鲁棒优化求解时间偏移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以跨视角稳定的物体级 3D 关系替代易受遮挡和快速运动干扰的像素级证据」的思路，可能与 LVR 中实体关系表示及视觉证据筛选、线索互补（深度/分割失效时改用 2D 运动）有概念联系，可供核查；但任务是相机同步，不涉及 latent 推理状态生成，联系较远。
